name: Evening Primrose

facts.how: Root cooked; young leaves cooked; flowers raw
facts.when: Cool seasons for root and leaves

caution: Eat the first-year root cooked and the young leaves cooked; both are peppery and best not eaten in quantity raw. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A first-year rosette becomes a tall stalk of yellow flowers that open at dusk. The useful root is the fleshy taproot of the first-year plant.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The cooked root is peppery and a little nutty, a wild parsnip of sorts; the young leaves cook down and the flowers garnish a plate.
